authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the step-by-step construction of the line graph (also called the edge graph or adjoint graph) of an undirected graph, presented in three labeled sub-panels (a, b, c). Panel a), titled ‘Original graph’, shows a 6-node undirected graph whose nodes are filled orange-colored circles labeled 1 through 6, connected by thin black undirected edges. Panel b) shows the intermediate transformation step, annotated with the instruction ‘Add new node at each original edge’: a new teal circle is placed at the position of each edge of the original graph, with the original 6 nodes still visible. Panel c), titled ‘Edge graph’, shows the resulting line graph, in which each new node is labeled by the pair of original endpoint nodes it represents (e.g., ‘2/3’, ‘1/4’, ‘4/6’, ‘1/6’, ‘4/5’, ‘2/5’, ‘1/3’), and the annotation ‘Connect new nodes if original edges shared node’ explains the rule for drawing new edges between them. All graph nodes across panels use the same teal fill color (#a0d9d3) and thin black outlines, while edges are drawn as plain black lines without arrowheads. This figure introduces the adjoint or line graph transformation, in which each edge of the original graph becomes a node in the new graph, a construct used in edge-centric graph neural network architectures.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate the adjoint graph construction step by step: first place a new node at each original edge, then draw edges between new nodes whenever the corresponding original edges shared a node
- Click an edge in the original graph to highlight the corresponding node in the edge graph and show the shared-node connections it generates
- Toggle between the Original graph and Edge graph panels to compare the structure before and after the adjoint transformation

discrepancies: The large grey transition arrows and their associated instructional text ('Add new node...', 'Connect new nodes...') present at the bottom of the source image are omitted from the drawing canvas.
The panel labels ('a)', 'b)', 'c)') and titles ('Original graph', 'Edge graph') have been moved into the interactive UI panel rather than being rendered as text directly on the figure.
evaluation.notes: An exceptionally well-executed interactive adaptation. The step-by-step player perfectly captures the three states of the original static figure, and the addition of a click-to-highlight 'Phantom view' connecting the edge graph back to the original graph topology is a brilliant pedagogical touch.
action_items: Render the step titles ('a) Original graph', 'c) Edge graph') directly onto the SVG canvas at the top of the appropriate steps, rather than only displaying them in the UI panel.

Draw the large grey directional arrows and their instructional text ('Add new node...', 'Connect new nodes...') at the bottom of the canvas during the transition steps to visually match the instructional cues in the source image.

feedback.rationale: The scores are exceptionally high (mostly 5s), the core concept and interactions are perfectly executed, and the discrepancies are only minor styling and labeling omissions that don't detract from the figure's utility.
